## How it works

- [statement] The October 30 Atlas configuration and transition pages specify embedded config servers at ten or fewer shards and dedicated config servers above ten when Atlas-managed config servers apply. A 7.0-to-8.0 upgrade alone preserves the existing type; shard-count changes trigger selection. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-additional-settings/ · keywords: Config shard (embedded config server) cost trade-off · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/transition-to-dedicated-config-servers/
- [statement] Atlas snapshot restores require the destination config-server type to match the source type: embedded-to-embedded or dedicated-to-dedicated. Include this compatibility restriction when evaluating a topology change for savings. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-additional-settings/ · keywords: Config shard (embedded config server) cost trade-off
- [statement] As of the October 30, 2026 Atlas pages, new clusters with Atlas-managed config servers use embedded servers at ten or fewer shards and dedicated servers above ten. Shard-count changes trigger reselection, subject to feature exceptions. The server manual instead says more than five shards; verify the effective policy before budgeting an expansion. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-additional-settings/ · keywords: Config shard (embedded config server) cost trade-off · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/transition-to-dedicated-config-servers/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/config-shard/
- [statement] Percona favors separate replica-set roles for large clusters because the relative infrastructure saving becomes small. MinervaDB independently recommends separation for latency-sensitive workloads to avoid metadata and user I/O competing in one WiredTiger cache. These are operational recommendations, not comparative performance benchmarks. (medium confidence) — https://www.percona.com/blog/scaling-smarter-what-you-have-missed-in-mongodb-8-0/ · keywords: Config shard (embedded config server) cost trade-off · also: https://minervadb.com/mongodb-8-3-high-availability-and-scalability/
- [statement] The reviewed sources support an avoided-replica-set cost mechanism but do not establish a universal dollar or percentage saving for Atlas. Estimate the actual difference from the cluster configuration, region and workload, including conversion headroom. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-additional-settings/ · keywords: Config shard (embedded config server) cost trade-off · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/scaling-smarter-what-you-have-missed-in-mongodb-8-0/, https://minervadb.com/mongodb-8-3-high-availability-and-scalability/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Percona recommends separating config-server and data roles for large clusters because maintenance isolation becomes more valuable and the relative infrastructure saving shrinks. MinervaDB independently recommends separating metadata I/O for larger or latency-sensitive deployments; its three-shard advice is an operator recommendation, not an Atlas service limit. (medium confidence) — https://www.percona.com/blog/scaling-smarter-what-you-have-missed-in-mongodb-8-0/ · keywords: Config shard (embedded config server) cost trade-off · also: https://minervadb.com/mongodb-8-3-high-availability-and-scalability/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Embedded config servers reduce infrastructure overhead by combining roles in one replica set. Dedicated config servers add a separate replica set, so the saving is avoided infrastructure rather than a published fixed percentage discount. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-additional-settings/ · keywords: Config shard (embedded config server) cost trade-off · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/scaling-smarter-what-you-have-missed-in-mongodb-8-0/
- [statement] Dedicated config servers isolate metadata from application data. The self-managed manual identifies Queryable Encryption collections and on-premises queryable backups as features requiring dedicated config servers; a development topology tutorial repeats these restrictions, so it is corroborating coverage rather than another independent finding. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/config-shard/ · keywords: Config shard (embedded config server) cost trade-off · also: https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-compose-a-sharded-mongodb-cluster-with-docker/
- [statement] With three-member replica sets, a two-shard deployment uses six mongod processes with an embedded config server versus nine with a dedicated config-server replica set. This is a conditional node-count comparison, not a measured 33% reduction in the total bill. (medium confidence) — https://minervadb.com/mongodb-8-3-high-availability-and-scalability/ · keywords: Config shard (embedded config server) cost trade-off · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-additional-settings/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Starting with MongoDB 8.0, a config shard can hold both application data and cluster metadata. Combining these roles avoids a separate config-server replica set and reduces infrastructure overhead, especially in small clusters. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/config-shard/ · keywords: Config shard (embedded config server) cost trade-off · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/scaling-smarter-what-you-have-missed-in-mongodb-8-0/, https://www.linux-magazin.de/ausgaben/2024/08/mongodb/
- [statement] MongoDB states that config shards have no measurable performance impact at low shard counts. The cited manual provides no workload, latency percentile, hardware configuration, or benchmark results establishing a general guarantee. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/config-shard/ · keywords: Config shard (embedded config server) cost trade-off
- [statement] Atlas documents dedicated config servers as a three-node M30 replica set. During embedded-to-dedicated conversion, Atlas drains config-0, adds a replacement data shard to preserve the target shard count, and scales config-0 down to M30. The resulting topology therefore includes an additional replica set to budget for. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-additional-settings/ · keywords: Config shard (embedded config server) cost trade-off · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/transition-to-dedicated-config-servers/
- [statement] Atlas transitions are online but can take hours to days for large datasets. Receiving shards need CPU, memory and I/O headroom; Atlas blocks other long-running plans, including tier and storage changes, while the transition runs. Pre-scale receiving shards if necessary. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/transition-to-dedicated-config-servers/ · keywords: Config shard (embedded config server) cost trade-off · also: https://minervadb.com/mongodb-8-3-high-availability-and-scalability/
- [statement] Atlas config-server type changes have feature gates. Search/Vector Search pins the existing type; unsharded Queryable Encryption blocks automatic migration. Global Clusters always use dedicated config servers, and Atlas replica-set-to-sharded conversions initially use dedicated config servers regardless of the managed setting. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/transition-to-dedicated-config-servers/ · keywords: Config shard (embedded config server) cost trade-off · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-additional-settings/
- [statement] The manual documents sh.isConfigShardEnabled() and listShards through mongos as ways to identify a config shard. A listShards entry whose _id is config identifies the combined role; replica-set names alone are unreliable indicators in Atlas. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/config-shard/ · keywords: Config shard (embedded config server) cost trade-off · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-additional-settings/
- [statement] Embedded-config savings are conditional on Atlas feature eligibility: Global Clusters always use dedicated config servers, and converting an Atlas replica set to a sharded cluster initially yields dedicated config servers. Search/Vector Search, unsharded time-series collections and unsharded Queryable Encryption can block automatic config-type transitions. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-additional-settings/ · keywords: Config shard (embedded config server) cost trade-off · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/transition-to-dedicated-config-servers/
